subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What native SKILL.md trust model should OpenClaw adopt for third-party skills: advisory verification only, runtime signature enforcement, or staged enforcement tied to capability policy?
rationale: This decides the permanent issuer/trust-root model, signature envelope, revocation behavior, unsigned defaults, capability restrictions, and upgrade compatibility for instructions loaded into agent context.

options.title: Adopt Staged Runtime Trust
options.body: Define a versioned digest/signature contract, persist trusted metadata at install/update, then add loader-time warn/strict enforcement and unsigned capability restrictions with migration guidance.

options.title: Keep Verification Advisory
options.body: Keep ClawHub verify output and install provenance as user-visible trust signals without runtime blocking until maintainers define a stronger enforcement API.

options.title: Split Design First
options.body: Track issuer/signature format, ClawHub metadata, loader checks, capability policy, and migration as separate owner-reviewed design tasks before code work.

recommendation.title: Adopt Staged Runtime Trust
recommendation.body: Define a versioned digest/signature contract, persist trusted metadata at install/update, then add loader-time warn/strict enforcement and unsigned capability restrictions with migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest visible product/security review signal on this issue and recent adjacent ClawHub/security-boundary history.
